Method of Attack: Using sequential device IDs with default passwords to allow attackers to scan and take control of devices remotely
Hijacking cameras by cycling through sequential device IDs and using default passwords to connect to vendor's backend cloud server
Supply-chain vulnerability due to white-label devices rebranded and resold by multiple vendors
Exploitation of insecure cloud-based remote control system allowing unauthorized access to video streams
Impacted Systems: Android apps using the Yoosee app
Devices from Shenzhen Gwelltimes Technology Co., Ltd.
Attack Vector: Internet scans for sequential device IDs
Use of default passwords such as '123', '123456', '888888'
Mobile app requiring device ID and default password to connect to cloud backend
Remote cloud server connections based on device ID and last reported IP address
Indicators of Compromise: Yoosee app with over 1 million installs on Google Play Store
Reports of hijacked baby monitors and security cameras
Use of the Yoosee app to manage devices
Devices traced to Shenzhen Gwelltimes Technology Co., Ltd.
